note.title: Regular present patterns
note.overview: This lesson contains 54 enabled questions. It teaches Regular present patterns through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Regular present patterns.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Regular patterns depend on the subject.
Silent endings still matter in writing.
Apply the pattern inside a complete sentence.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « je » form in the -er: jouer column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives je → joue for -er: jouer. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « tu » form in the -er: jouer column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives tu → joues for -er: jouer. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « il / elle / on » form in the -er: jouer column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives il / elle / on → joue for -er: jouer. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « nous » form in the -er: jouer column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives nous → jouons for -er: jouer. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « vous » form in the -er: jouer column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives vous → jouez for -er: jouer. The subject decides the written ending.

commonMistakes: Do not change a correct answer into an error just because the learner also wrote the subject.
